parameters.toolDescription:
Retrieves full detail for a single session by ID.

Parameters:
- id (string, required): Exact session UUID
parameters.query: SELECT s.id, s.participant_name, s.role, s.company_type, s.technical_ability, s.ai_usage, s.ai_usage_evidence, s.using_n8n_for, s.session_summary, s.profile_summary, s.approved, s.project_id, s.created_at, s.updated_at FROM session s WHERE s.id::text = '{{ $fromAI("id") }}' LIMIT 1

parameters.toolDescription:
Lists sessions with lightweight metadata.

Returns: id, participant_name, role, company_type, created_at, and project_name (returned alongside participant_name and created_at via a join on the project table).

Parameters (all optional):
- project_id, participant_name, role, company_type, approved, limit (default 10)
parameters.query: SELECT s.id, s.participant_name, s.role, s.company_type, s.created_at, p.name AS project_name FROM session s LEFT JOIN project p ON s.project_id = p.id WHERE ('{{ $fromAI("project_id") }}' = '' OR s.project_id::text = '{{ $fromAI("project_id") }}') AND ('{{ $fromAI("participant_name") }}' = '' OR s.participant_name ILIKE '%' || '{{ $fromAI("participant_name") }}' || '%') AND ('{{ $fromAI("role") }}' = '' OR s.role ILIKE '%' || '{{ $fromAI("role") }}' || '%') AND ('{{ $fromAI("company_type") }}' = '' OR s.company_type ILIKE '%' || '{{ $fromAI("company_type") }}' || '%') AND ('{{ $fromAI("approved") }}' = '' OR s.approved::text = '{{ $fromAI("approved") }}') ORDER BY s.created_at DESC

parameters.toolDescription:
Retrieves jobs-to-be-done linked to sessions with clips.

Parameters (all optional):
- session_id, project_id, theme, limit (default 20)
parameters.query: SELECT j.id, j.content, j.theme, j.evidence, j.clips, s.id AS session_id, s.participant_name FROM job j JOIN session_jobs sj ON sj.job_id = j.id JOIN session s ON s.id = sj.session_id WHERE j.deleted IS NOT TRUE AND ('{{ $fromAI("session_id") }}' = '' OR sj.session_id::text = '{{ $fromAI("session_id") }}') AND ('{{ $fromAI("project_id") }}' = '' OR s.project_id::text = '{{ $fromAI("project_id") }}') AND ('{{ $fromAI("theme") }}' = '' OR j.theme ILIKE '%' || '{{ $fromAI("theme") }}' || '%') ORDER BY j.created_at DESC

parameters.toolDescription:
Retrieves opportunities linked to sessions with clips.

Parameters (all optional):
- session_id, project_id, limit (default 20)
parameters.query: SELECT o.id, o.content, o.clips, s.id AS session_id, s.participant_name FROM opportunity o JOIN session_opportunities so ON so.opportunity_id = o.id JOIN session s ON s.id = so.session_id WHERE o.deleted IS NOT TRUE AND ('{{ $fromAI("session_id") }}' = '' OR so.session_id::text = '{{ $fromAI("session_id") }}') AND ('{{ $fromAI("project_id") }}' = '' OR s.project_id::text = '{{ $fromAI("project_id") }}') ORDER BY o.created_at DESC

parameters.toolDescription:
Retrieves full detail for a single project by ID including the research script.

Parameters:
- id (string, required): Exact project UUID
parameters.query: SELECT id, name, type, script, research_date, created_at, updated_at FROM project WHERE id::text = '{{ $fromAI("id") }}' LIMIT 1

parameters.toolDescription:
Lists projects with lightweight metadata.

Parameters (all optional):
- name (string), type (string), limit (number, default 20)
parameters.query: SELECT id, name, type, research_date, created_at FROM project WHERE ('{{ $fromAI("name") }}' = '' OR name ILIKE '%' || '{{ $fromAI("name") }}' || '%') AND ('{{ $fromAI("type") }}' = '' OR type::text = '{{ $fromAI("type") }}') ORDER BY created_at DESC

parameters.toolDescription: Searches Slack messages for team research discussions, synthesis notes, and internal insights. Use AFTER searching sessions with vectors. Pass a natural language query. Returns matching messages with author, channel, and date metadata. Label results as [Slack - #channel-name].

Searches Gong sales/customer call transcripts for prospect or customer quotes — pricing reactions, objections, feature asks, deal feedback, competitive positioning. Use AFTER sessions/Slack/Community when the question is specifically about sales calls. Pass a natural language query. Returns top-K matching documents — each is either a call summary (doc_type="summary") or a transcript chunk (doc_type="transcript") — with metadata: call_id, doc_type, title, url, embed_url_base, scheduled_at, meeting_system, primary_user_id. Chunk content contains inline [seconds.fraction] markers (e.g. [475.14]) — these are timestamps within the call. Use them with embed_url_base to build deep links: {embed_url_base}&from={int_seconds}&to={int_seconds + 60}. IMPORTANT: only quote external participants (prospects/customers). Never quote n8n internal staff. Use get_gong_call to check parties[].affiliation if uncertain. Label results as [Gong - {title}, {scheduled_at}]. To pull deeper context (full raw call payload), call get_gong_call with the call_id.

Retrieves the full raw payload for a single Gong call by call_id, including the complete transcript, parties (with affiliation: Internal/External), content (brief, key points, outline, highlights, trackers), metaData, and collaboration. Use after `gong` returns matching calls when you need deeper context than the search snippet, or when you need to check who is internal (n8n) vs external (prospect/customer) before quoting.

Parameters:
- id (string, required): Exact Gong call_id
parameters.query: SELECT call_id, scheduled_at, primary_user_id, meeting_system, data, ingested_at FROM public.gong_calls WHERE call_id = '{{ $fromAI("id") }}' LIMIT 1

parameters.description:
Live search of the n8n community forum (community.n8n.io, Discourse). Returns a structured list of TOPICS with title, url, category, tags, solved status, reply/view/like counts, dates, and an excerpt. Does NOT return full post bodies — call get_forum_thread for that.

Parameters (all optional except query):
- query (string, required): keyword(s) to search for. Use exact terms when relevant (error messages, node names like "googleSheets", version numbers).
- category (string): category slug or name (e.g. "questions", "feature-requests", "built-with-n8n", "tips-tricks").
- tags (string): comma-separated tag list (e.g. "credentials,workflow-building"). Topics must have ALL listed tags.
- status (string): one of solved, unsolved, open, closed, archived, noreplies, single_user, public.
- after (string): YYYY-MM-DD; only topics created after this date.
- before (string): YYYY-MM-DD; only topics created before this date.
- min_likes (number/string): minimum like count.
- order (string): one of latest, likes, views, latest_topic. Default is relevance ranking.
- page (string): page number, default 1. ~30 results per page.

value.query: ={{ $fromAI('query', 'Keyword(s) to search for. Use exact terms when relevant.', 'string') }}
value.category: ={{ $fromAI('category', 'Optional category slug (e.g. questions, feature-requests). Empty for any.', 'string') }}
value.status: ={{ $fromAI('status', 'Optional: solved | unsolved | open | closed | archived | noreplies. Empty for any.', 'string') }}
value.order: ={{ $fromAI('order', 'Optional: latest | likes | views | latest_topic. Empty for relevance.', 'string') }}

parameters.description:
Fetches a single n8n community forum thread by topic_id (from search_forum or forum_store results). Returns the original post (the question), the accepted answer (if any), and top replies — already cleaned of HTML and trimmed for context. Each post includes post_number, url, username, staff flag, trust_level, like_count, body. Use sparingly — one thread is heavy.

Parameters:
- topic_id (string, required): The numeric topic ID.

parameters.toolDescription:
Semantic vector search over n8n community forum POSTS (community.n8n.io). Each result is a single forum post (the original post, accepted answer, or a reply) — NOT a whole thread. Multiple posts from the same thread can come back as separate hits; group by topic_id when synthesizing.

Use for fuzzy/conceptual queries where exact wording is unknown ("frustration with credentials", "people excited about AI agents").

Result metadata:
- POST-LEVEL: post_id, post_number, post_type (original_post|accepted_answer|reply), post_url, post_username, post_staff (bool), post_trust_level, post_score, post_like_count, post_created_at
- TOPIC-LEVEL (denormalized on every row): topic_id, topic_title, topic_url, topic_category, topic_tags, topic_solved, topic_created_at, topic_last_posted_at, topic_reply_count, topic_views, topic_like_count, topic_accepted_post_id, topic_original_username
- TOPIC CLASSIFICATION (from Claude Haiku, applied to every post in a topic): sentiment (very_negative..very_positive), feedback_type (bug | feature_request | usability_issue | performance_issue | integration_issue | pricing_feedback | documentation_feedback | support_request | praise | comparison | offtopic), summary

The content field is the body of that single post. To read the full thread including posts not returned here, call get_forum_thread with the topic_id. Cite as [Forum: {topic_category}, {post_created_at}, ✓ solved if topic_solved](post_url) and attribute to post_username (note "(n8n staff)" if post_staff is true).

parameters.description: Reads eval cases or eval results from the Darwin evaluation system. Use this to check what eval cases exist, view results from eval runs, or check scores. Parameters: table (required, either "cases" to list eval test cases, or "results" to view eval run scores and verdicts), run_id (optional, filter results to a specific eval run), case_id (optional, filter to a specific case).

Triggers a full eval run across all stored eval cases. Dispatches all cases in parallel and optionally posts results to a Slack thread when complete. Parameters: slack_channel (optional, Slack channel ID to post results to when complete), slack_thread_ts (optional, Slack thread timestamp to reply to with results). If both slack_channel and slack_thread_ts are provided, results will be posted to that thread automatically when all cases finish. Otherwise results can be checked with the read_evals tool.

Triggers the Integration test suite: calls every connected tool (Darwin's and Builder's) with canonical inputs and checks deterministic assertions. Results are stored in the Darwin Integration Results table and a summary is returned (optionally posted to the Slack thread). Use when asked to run integration checks/tests or verify tool health.
Reads Integration test cases or results. Parameters: table (required, "cases" or "results"), case_id (optional filter), run_id (optional filter).

Adds an Integration test case (a deterministic check of one connected tool). Parameters: case_id (unique slug), target_type ("workflow" or "sql"), target (workflow name e.g. SessionSearch, or tool name for sql), agent ("darwin" or "builder"), description, inputs (JSON string of canonical inputs; for sql type: {"sql": "..."}), assertions (JSON string array, e.g. [{"type":"row_count","op":">=","value":1}], [{"type":"exact","path":"name","value":"x"}], [{"type":"field_exists","path":"id"}], [{"type":"contains","value":"text"}]).

Triggers the Unit test suite: deterministic checks of non-agent workflows (e.g. SlackMarkdown, SanitizeMemory). Results are stored in the Darwin Unit Results table and a summary is returned (optionally posted to the Slack thread). Use when asked to run unit checks/tests.
Reads Unit test cases or results. Parameters: table (required, "cases" or "results"), case_id (optional filter), run_id (optional filter).

Adds a Unit test case (deterministic check of a non-agent workflow). Parameters: case_id (unique slug), target (SlackMarkdown or SanitizeMemory), description, inputs (JSON string), assertions (JSON string array, e.g. [{"type":"exact","value":{"output":"..."}}]).
